description: The figure shows two vertically stacked bar charts illustrating “% point difference” values across XLM-R model layers (including a “concat” condition) for two settings or series distinguished by color (top chart in light blue, bottom chart in darker blue). In both charts, the category axis is horizontal and lists layer indices in ascending order from 0 through 12, followed by a final category labeled “concat”; the bottom chart explicitly labels this axis as “layer,” while the top chart places the text “XLM-R” beneath the plot area. The value axis is vertical, labeled “% point difference,” uses a linear scale, and spans from about 0 at the top down to approximately −10 at the bottom, with regularly spaced tick marks at 0, −2, −4, −6, −8, and −10. In the top (light-blue) chart, the bars for layers 0–5 extend downward with approximate values of −10.5 (layer 0), −8.6 (layer 1), −7.6 (layer 2), −5.1 (layer 3), −3.9 (layer 4), and −2.5 (layer 5); layers 6–8 are small negatives around −0.8, −0.8, and −0.3; layers 9–10 are near zero and slightly positive (around +0.1); layer 11 is slightly negative (about −0.2); layer 12 is around −1.2; and “concat” is slightly positive (about +0.4). In the bottom (dark-blue) chart, layers 0–5 are negative with approximate values of −9.6 (layer 0), −9.6 (layer 1), −8.2 (layer 2), −5.8 (layer 3), −3.5 (layer 4), and −2.2 (layer 5); layers 6–9 are small negatives around −0.6, −0.5, −0.6, and −0.4; layers 10–11 are small positives around +0.3 and +0.4; layer 12 is slightly negative (about −0.3); and “concat” is slightly positive (about +0.4). The bars are not shown as grouped or stacked within each category, there is no visible legend explaining the two panels, and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the differing fill colors between the two charts.
